check.population: every domain type, business rule and context boundary in the domain layer
check.freshness: a verdict stands until a domain type, a rule's location or a context boundary changes
check.refusal: the layer rule or the domain test fails when a rule or a model leaves its context or its aggregate
check.observation: where each business rule and invariant is enforced, read from source and the domain tests
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the domain model, which decides the context and the aggregate every rule belongs to

distinctFrom.reason: Domain-driven design models software on the domain's language, while event-driven architecture connects services through published events.

records.name: Domain-Driven Design (DDD)
records.definition: A convention of modeling software on the business domain's own language, split into bounded contexts with a domain model in each.

records.name: Domain Model
records.definition: A formal definition of the business concepts, rules and invariants of one context, written as types with behavior.

exemplar.before:
type Foo = { status: string; count: number };
function closeFoo(foo: Foo) { foo.status = "closed"; }

distinctFrom.reason: A bounded context fixes meaning inside one boundary, while relationship semantics fixes the meaning of each link between boundaries.

records.name: Bounded Context
records.definition: A rule or precondition that each domain model holds inside one explicit boundary, where its terms have one meaning.

exemplar.before:
type FooStatus = "A" | "D";
function priceBar(status: FooStatus) { return status === "A" ? 10 : 0; }

records.name: Context Mapping
records.definition: The activity of recording how bounded contexts relate, including which one is upstream and how their models translate.

records.name: Anti-Corruption Layer
records.definition: A design pattern that translates an external system's model into the local domain's terms at the boundary.
detected_by: external DTOs used in domain layer

distinctFrom.reason: Explicit boundaries declare a module's interface and owner, while declared jurisdiction declares which roots and files a naming gate governs.
Explicit boundaries fix where one module ends, while abstraction fixes how a concept is expressed without its detail.
Explicit boundaries govern access between modules, while encapsulation governs changes to one object's state.
Explicit boundaries are the declared interfaces, while governance holds decisions to shared policy.
Explicit boundaries give each module one public interface, while a single source of truth gives each fact one owning definition.
Explicit boundaries declare the interface, while independence is testing and deploying a module without its neighbors.
Explicit boundaries declare each module's interface and owner, while modularity is the division into modules itself.
Explicit boundaries declare interfaces, while separation of concerns decides which concerns sit on each side of them.
Explicit boundaries declare interfaces, while single responsibility limits what sits behind one to one reason to change.

records.name: Explicit Boundaries
records.definition: A design rule that each module declares its public interface and owner, and other modules reach it only through that interface.

exemplar.before:
import { fooDatabase } from "../../foo/infrastructure/database";
export function loadBar(id: string) { return fooDatabase.query(id); }
exemplar.after:
export interface FooGateway { find(id: FooId): Promise<FooSnapshot>; }
export function loadBar(id: FooId, foos: FooGateway) { return foos.find(id); }

records.name: Aggregate
records.definition: A design pattern that groups entities under one root, which is the only entry point and keeps the group's invariants.
detected_by: cross-entity invariant checks scattered in services

records.name: Value Object
records.definition: A design pattern that models a domain value as an immutable, self-validating object compared by its attributes.
detected_by: repeated validation of the same primitive shape

exemplar.before: function priceFoo(amount: number, currency: string) { return { amount, currency }; }

distinctFrom.reason: An entity is known by an identity that outlives its attributes, while a value object is known only by its attributes.

records.name: Entity
records.definition: A design pattern that models a domain object by a stable identity, which stays the same while its attributes change.
detected_by: equality by field value where identity is meant

exemplar.before:
type Foo = { id: string; name: string; status: string };
foo.status = "active";

distinctFrom.reason: A domain service holds a stateless rule spanning entities, while an aggregate holds entities and their invariants under one root.

records.name: Domain Service
records.definition: A design pattern that places a domain rule spanning several entities in a stateless service named in the domain's language.
